newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends lower as banks stay in dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends lower as banks stay in dlrs.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed down on Wednesday against the dollar, despite recovering from the day's low, as banks preferred to hold the dollar due to its overseas strength, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.58 to the dollar after opening at 58.54 and falling to a low of 58.63, they said.

"The rupee regined some strength after an early decline due to import covering, but could not recover totally because many banks prefered to hang on to the dollar which is rising overseas," said a Bank of Ceylon dealer.
Overnight call money rates closed at 16 percent after a day of volatile movement when they rose to 22, dealers said.
"Call money was volatile due to seasonal withdrawals of cash for next week's Sinhala and Tamil New Year," said the Bank of Ceylon dealer.
The Bank of Ceylon entering with a lending position brought a degree of calm to the money market, dealers said.
